Article Title: Delhi pollution crackdown: Hotspots to be mapped, pending road works get Oct 31 deadline
Article Text:
A thick layer of smog engulfs the India Gate and Kartavya Path as pollution level deteriorates, in New Delhi.

Hotspots to get source-specific action plans

October 31 target for pending road works

Construction, waste burning face tighter action

Illegal parking and encroachments targeted

Patparganj gets special focus

Future roads to minimise exposed soil

NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has stepped up its crackdown on air pollution, directing district administrations to map pollution hotspots, identify sources within a three-kilometre radius and assign agencies specific corrective measures and deadlines. The government has also set October 31 as the target for completing pending road and civil works, wherever feasible. It ordered tighter action against road dust, construction pollution, waste burning, illegal parking and traffic congestion.The directions were issued during district-level review meetings chaired by Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa for East, North-East, South-East and South Delhi. Officials were told to use AQI monitoring data to identify problem areas, assess the sources driving pollution and take immediate action at the ground level.District administrations will map pollution hotspots based on data from AQI monitoring stations. Each hotspot will then be assessed for sources such as road dust, traffic congestion, vehicular emissions, construction and demolition activity, unauthorised parking, open or uncovered areas and biomass or waste burning.Where applicable, pollution-generating activities within a three-kilometre radius of each hotspot will also be examined.Authorities will prepare source-wise action plans setting out the remedial measure, the agency responsible and the timeline for implementation.Locations recording high levels of PM10 and PM2.5 will receive focused attention, particularly areas with heavy traffic, heavy-vehicle parking, significant road dust and congestion. Such locations will be inspected for their pollution sources and immediate remedial action will be taken.The government has directed agencies to complete pending civil works on priority and by October 31, wherever feasible.These include pothole repairs, treatment and development of brown areas and other road and roadside works. Officials have also been told to maintain completed works properly to reduce road-dust generation.Where essential works cannot be completed because other projects are still underway, agencies will have to continue water sprinkling and other dust-suppression measures until the road surface is restored.The government has directed agencies to strictly enforce dust-control norms at construction and demolition sites. Violations will attract stringent action under applicable rules.The ban on biomass burning will also be enforced without exception. Preventive measures will be strengthened against the open burning of garbage, plastic and rubber waste, textile and fibre waste, industrial and organic residues, scrap and other combustible material.Officials were also directed to remove illegal encroachments from roads and public spaces where they contribute to congestion and obstruct traffic movement.The move is aimed at improving traffic flow and reducing pollution caused by idling vehicles and prolonged traffic movement.At Anand Vihar Bus Terminal, agencies have been directed to step up enforcement against unauthorised parking of buses and heavy vehicles. Cranes will be deployed wherever required to remove or tow such vehicles.Patparganj Industrial Area was identified for area-specific measures targeting road dust, traffic congestion and vehicular emissions.Agencies have been directed to maintain continuous water sprinkling and dust-control measures at vulnerable locations, particularly where road or allied works are underway.For future applicable works, departments have been directed to incorporate end-to-end carpeting or paving of roads and relevant roadside areas wherever technically feasible and in accordance with applicable specifications.The aim is to reduce exposed soil and unpaved surfaces that can contribute to road dust.The government has stressed closer coordination between departments and agencies, with responsibility for individual pollution-control measures clearly assigned.The meetings involved area MLAs, district magistrates, deputy commissioners of police, MCD deputy commissioners and senior officials from various departments.Officials from the Revenue Department, DPCC, PWD, MCD, Traffic Police, DSIIDC, I&FC, DJB, DMRC, NHAI and other agencies were involved in the coordinated effort.The minister also directed ground teams to maintain regular vigilance at vulnerable locations and take immediate action against violations. DPCC and enforcement agencies were asked to impose stringent penalties, including heavy challans wherever applicable.Officials were further told to ensure prompt resolution of citizen complaints, particularly those received through Helpline 311.
Article Summary: District administrations will map pollution hotspots based on data from AQI monitoring stations. Each hotspot will be assessed for sources such as road dust, traffic congestion, vehicular emissions, construction and demolition activity, unauthorised parking, open or uncovered areas and biomass or waste burning.

NEW DELHI: Indian Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh and Japan Air Self-Defence Force Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita took sorties on Tejas fighter aircraft on Sunday.This comes amid the ongoing Indo-Japan bilateral air exercise 'Veer Guardian-2026' at Air Force Station Jodhpur in Rajasthan.The IAF is participating with a mix of frontline combat aircraft, including the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale fighter jets, while the JASDF has deployed its F-2A fighter aircraft.The exercise, which began on September 9 and will continue till September 22, involves advanced operational missions, mission planning and professional exchanges between personnel of the two air forces.The participation of Japanese fighter aircraft in the exercise marks the first time JASDF combat aircraft have operated from Indian soil.Earlier, on September 10, defence minister Rajnath Singh described Japan sending its fighter aircraft to participate in Exercise Veer Guardian as a "significant milestone" for the India-Japan defence partnership.In a post on X, he said the maiden visit of Japan Air Self-Defence Force fighter aircraft to India reflected growing trust and a shared commitment to peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.He also recalled his "highly productive discussions" with his Japanese counterpart in New Delhi last month, saying exchanges such as Exercise Veer Guardian would further strengthen cooperation between the two countries.The Indian Air Force had welcomed the Japanese F-2 fighter jets to Jodhpur on September 8 ahead of the exercise. During the 14-day drill, air warriors from the two countries are undertaking advanced operational missions and engaging in extensive professional interactions.

Article Title: Congress calls SIR 'Shah Instigated Removal', flags large-scale voter deletions
Article Text:
Jairam Ramesh attacks Union home minister Amit Shah.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday took a swipe at Union home minister Amit Shah over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that it was a "Shah Instigated Removal" of voters.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said the Election Commission began Phase 1 of the SIR process in Bihar in June 2025, followed by Phase 2 in November 2025 across nine states and three Union Territories.According to Jairam Ramesh, 7.8 crore names were deleted during the first two phases, amounting to 13% of the pre-SIR electoral roll.Jairam said Phase 3 began in 16 states and three Union Territories in mid-2026. Citing data from 12 states and two UTs, he claimed that 6.18 crore names had been deleted from a total of 36.06 crore voters."The deletion rate works out to over 17% 2. An additional 5.43 crore voters have been issued notices demanding additional documentation to have their names retained on the electoral roll. The risk of deletion rate works to another 15%. This is an unusually high proportion that reflects structural flaws in the entire SIR process," Jairam said.He questioned how such a large number of voters could still be required to undergo verification after the deletion of millions of names."Thus, a staggering 32% (or about one in three) of voters have had their names deleted or face risk of deletion," Jairam added.He cited Delhi, Chandigarh, Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya, Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Haryana, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Punjab as states and UTs where he claimed a significant proportion of voters had either been deleted or faced the risk of deletion.The Congress leader also alleged that large-scale deletions were disproportionately affecting voters from economically and socially disadvantaged sections. He further claimed that, in most major states, more women than men had been removed from electoral rolls during the SIR process.Jairam said the exercise had shifted the burden of verification from the state to citizens, who were being asked to produce documents that they may never have been issued. "A test that the overwhelming majority of citizens cannot pass is just a 'machine for exclusion'," he said."SIR is actually a massive Shah Instigated Removal of voters. It is an assault on our Constitution," he added.Tagging his statement on X, he wrote, "SIR is actually a Shah Instigated Removal of voters on a massive scale. Here is a statement on this brazen assault on our Constitution itself."Jairam also said voter lists facing deletion risks had been made publicly available in Karnataka, Telangana and Jharkhand, allowing voters to check their names. He claimed Delhi made its list public only on September 19, 2026, following public pressure, while other BJP-ruled states and Punjab had not done so.The Election Commission has maintained that the SIR, being conducted after 22 years, is aimed at cleaning electoral rolls by removing ineligible and duplicate entries while ensuring that all eligible citizens are included in the rolls.Opposition parties have alleged that the exercise could target voters who do not support the BJP and its allies. The allegations have been rejected by the Election Commission, which has defended the revision as an exercise to ensure accurate and legally eligible electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said the Election Commission began Phase 1 of the SIR process in Bihar in June 2025. He said 7.8 crore names were deleted during the first two phases, amounting to 13% of the pre-SIR electoral roll.

Punjab tourism minister Tarunpreet Singh Sond on Thursday said Punjab government's 'Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra' scheme has facilitated pilgrimage for 5,10,807 devotees to various religious destinations in and outside the state.He said the scheme aims to facilitate elderly residents who wish to visit religious places by providing them free travel and other essential facilities.The scheme was launched on November 9, 2025, and in its first phase, around four lakh pilgrims undertook journeys to Sri Amritsar Sahib, Sri Anandpur Sahib and Mata Naina Devi, he said.The scheme was expanded on August 12 to include additional religious destinations such as Shri Khatu Shyam-Salasar Balaji Dham, Haridwar-Rishikesh and Mathura-Vrindavan, he said.Under the expanded scheme, people aged 50 years and above are eligible to undertake the pilgrimage. NEW DELHI: India will manufacture indigenous high-speed or bullet trains with a design speed of 350 kmph (B35) by 2030, matching Japan's next-generation E10 series trains that are scheduled for production the same year, according to the railway ministry's Cabinet proposal seeking approval for the revised cost of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project.Cabinet has approved the revised cost of the project at over Rs 2 lakh crore, nearly double the original estimate prepared in 2015, and the expenditure of nearly Rs 1 lakh crore escalated cost will come from budgetary support.TOI has learnt that the ministry informed the Cabinet it has initiated the process to develop B35 trains after the Japanese side conveyed in Dec 2024 that production of existing E5 series trains was being phased out. It mentions that Japan indicated that production of E10 trains would begin in 2030 and they would be ready for operations by 2034. Officials said deployment of E10 trains would be explored when they become available.The ministry has said that manufacturing of indigenous B28 high-speed trains has been taken up and India will also develop its own Bharat Train Control System (BTCS). The move mirrors China's indigenous CTCS signalling and train control system, which manages speed, spacing and safety across conventional and high-speed rail networks.As per the ministry, sharp increase in project cost from earlier Rs 1.1 lakh crore is largely due to a more than three-fold rise in land acquisition cost to about Rs 19,700 crore; a nearly 50% increase in infrastructure cost to over Rs 1 lakh crore, and around 100% escalation in spending on trains and signalling systems compared with the 2015 estimate.The current cost of the project, excluding future Japanese trains, works out to around Rs 399 crore per km.Initially, the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor will operate with B28 trains having a design speed of 280 kmph, while their maximum operating speed will be "249 kmph". BEML has received contracts to manufacture 32 B28 trains.Two prototype trains are expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. BEML informed the BSE on Friday that it has received a separate Rs 5,400-crore contract to manufacture 15 additional B28 trains. The full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by Dec 2030.
Article Summary: India will manufacture indigenous high-speed or bullet trains with a design speed of 350 kmph (B35) The railway ministry's Cabinet proposal seeking approval for the revised cost of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project. Cabinet has approved revised cost at over Rs 2 lakh crore, nearly double original estimate.

Article Title: 'How is it possible?' Kejriwal and family get SIR notice in Delhi, EC responds
Article Text:
Kejriwal, family served notices under Delhi SIR

AAP questions names missing from voter list

EC responds to Kejriwal's SIR notice

NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and four members of his family have been served notices by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Notices have been issued to Kejriwal, his wife Sunita Kejriwal, son Pulkit Kejriwal, and parents Gobind Ram Kejriwal and Gita Devi . Kejriwal is a registered voter in the New Delhi-40 assembly constituency.According to Delhi Election Commission documents, Arvind Kejriwal and five members of his family are among 110 voters from ‘Part-51, KG Marg’ in the New Delhi assembly constituency who have been issued notices.The party questioned the move saying, “Is everything happening in this country just to keep the Supreme Lord happy? @ECISVEEP, how is it possible that the names of three-time Delhi Chief Minister @ArvindKejriwal Ji and his family members are missing from the Delhi voter list?”The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), New Delhi, has said notices were issued to former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his family members as their submitted Enumeration Forms did not contain sufficient details to establish their linkage with the electoral rolls of the last revision in their respective states.The ERO said, “the submitted Enumeration Forms were not complete in terms of details which would have enabled linkage of themselves with the electoral roll of the last revision of the respective states, which were not present in their submitted Enumeration Forms.”In a press statement, the ERO further said that notices were being issued in accordance with procedures established and communicated by the Election Commission to electors who could not be linked to the electoral roll of the last revision or whose linkage showed logical discrepancies.“ As per procedures established and communicated by ECI, Notices are being issued to the electors who could not be linked with the electoral roll of the last revision and those having logical discrepancies in their linking with the electoral roll of the last revision. Electors have to submit a reply/requisite documents to the ERO concerned on receipt of the Notice. Disposal of Notices will be completed by 29.10.2026,” the statement said.The Election Commission also said a notice was issued to Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta after her name appeared in the list of discrepancies during the ongoing SIR process.Following verification of her details and documents, her electoral entry was validated and will be included in the final electoral roll for AC-14 (Shalimar Bagh), scheduled to be published on November 4, 2026.The notices come amid the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026 exercise being conducted by the Delhi Election Commission. Nearly 47.6 lakh names were removed from Delhi's draft electoral roll published on August 31, but only a fraction of those affected have so far submitted Form 6 seeking re-inclusion.The window for filing claims and objections against the draft roll will remain open until September 30.The draft electoral roll contains 97.5 lakh electors, compared with 1.45 crore registered voters in Delhi when the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise began in June.Data showed that 62,583 Form 6 applications, including those from first-time voters seeking inclusion, had been submitted by September 15. The number rose to 68,043 by September 16.The 47.6 lakh electors excluded from Delhi's draft electoral roll have been categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others following the house-to-house verification exercise. Around 43.3 lakh were marked as absent or shifted, while about 2.8 lakh were categorised as dead and 1.4 lakh as duplicate entries.According to figures released by the Delhi election office for the claims and objections phase, 91,826 applications were received between August 31 and September 16.These included 22,715 Form 8 applications seeking correction or modification of existing electoral entries, 922 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names on grounds such as death, shifting, duplicate registration or ineligibility, and 146 Form 6A applications from overseas electors, besides Form 6 applications for inclusion in the electoral roll.After the claims and objections phase ends, officials will examine the applications and complete the disposal process by October 29. The final electoral roll under the SIR exercise is scheduled to be published on November 4.
Article Summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and four members of his family have been served notices by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office. Kejriwal is a registered voter in the New Delhi-40 assembly constituency. The party questioned the move saying, “Is everything happening in this country just to keep the Supreme Lord happy?”

Article Title: As monsoon withdrawal begins, season may end with 10% deficit
Article Text:
Monsoon withdrawal has begun

The deficit in rainfall

NEW DELHI: The southwest (summer) monsoon, which has so far reported a nationwide deficit of 15% in cumulative (June 1-Sept 19) rainfall, started withdrawing from west Rajasthan Saturday, as against the normal date of Sept 17, IMD has said.The line of withdrawal Saturday passed through Ramgarh, Mohangarh, Phalodi and Khajuwala. "Conditions are also favourable for further withdrawal from some more parts of Rajasthan and some parts of Punjab and Saurashtra and Kachchh over the next three-four days," said the Met department.The monsoon normally starts withdrawing from Sept 17 and the process ends on Oct 15 - a few days ahead of the onset of the winter monsoon in peninsular India.As many as 14 states, including Bihar, Punjab, Haryana and all five peninsular states, have reported a rain deficit of more than 20% so far. The current situation shows that the monsoon season is likely to end on Sept 30 with an overall deficit of more than 10% in the country as a whole - a level of rain deficiency which is considered a drought - even as the low pressure area and subsequent depression over east central Bay of Bengal may cause good rain in east India and coastal Odisha next week.Although the sowing of kharif (summer-sown) crops has progressed well despite the El Nino-linked rain deficit, it does not mean the crop sector is out of danger as regional variations and the skewed timing of rainfall may impact overall yield and sowing during next crop (rabi) season. El Nino, a climatic phenomenon involving the warming of ocean surface temperatures in central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is invariably associated with a harsh summer and weak monsoon in India.Acreage data Friday shows that though the overall sown area for all kharif crops has declined this year by just a little over 1%, water-intensive paddy - the most important seasonal crop that accounts for the most acreage - reported a decline of nearly 4% compared to the corresponding period last year.
Article Summary: The southwest (summer) monsoon started withdrawing from west Rajasthan Saturday. The monsoon normally starts withdrawing from Sept 17 and the process ends on Oct 15. The current situation shows that the monsoon season is likely to end on Sept 30 with an overall deficit of more than 10% in the country as a whole.

Article Title: BJP promise in its coastal bastion: Why DK Shivakumar put Tulu at centre in Mangaluru
Article Text:
DK Shivakumar cabinet meeting in Mangaluru

Eye on BJP's coastal bastion

More than just Tulu

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand."Today, we have decided to make Tulu applicable to Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts and declare it the state’s second additional administrative language," Shivakumar told reporters after a marathon cabinet meeting in Mangaluru.According to a cabinet note shared by the chief minister’s office, Tulu would be Karnataka’s "second additional administrative language" in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore at the time. Kannada is the state's most-widely spoken and its primary official language.This was also the first time a cabinet meeting was held in Mangaluru and not in Bengaluru.The political significance of Shivakumar taking his cabinet to Mangaluru becomes clearer against the BJP's electoral dominance in the region.Coastal Karnataka, particularly Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, has long been one of the BJP's strongest pockets in the state.In the 2023 Karnataka assembly election, BJP won 11 of the 13 seats across the two districts, taking all five seats in Udupi and six of the eight in Dakshina Kannada. The Congress won only two constituencies.This was despite Congress sweeping to power across Karnataka with 135 seats, against 66 for the BJP.The BJP's hold remained intact in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won both parliamentary seats covering the region, with Brijesh Chowta defeating Congress's Padmaraj R by over 64,000 votes in Dakshina Kannada. Kota Srinivas Poojary won Udupi-Chikkamagaluru by more than 2.5 lakh votes.The BJP responded to the Tulu announcement by alleging that Shivakumar was "peddling soft Hindutva to make a dent in the BJP’s vote bank.""Shivakumar has never made any secret of his firm belief in Hinduism and frequently visits temples, performs rituals publicly and quotes scriptures. He is now peddling soft Hindutva. This was also evident from his rendition of 'Namaste Sada Vatsale' inside the Karnataka assembly," a BJP leader told PTI, referring to an August 2025 incident in which Shivakumar sang a few lines of the RSS anthem.The RSS is the BJP's ideological mentor.But there is a political twist to the Tulu issue itself. The BJP had previously taken up the demand while in power in Karnataka.In January 2023, the then BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai constituted a committee to examine granting Tulu the status of a second official language in the state, months before the assembly election.Significantly, Shivakumar’s announcements went beyond granting Tulu the status of a second administrative language.The Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru marked the Shivakumar government’s first meeting outside Bengaluru, the state capital. Shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the region’s contribution and address its development needs.The chief minister added that a draft notification would soon be issued to invite public feedback on renaming the Dakshina Kannada district to Mangaluru district.He also announced a host of policies for the coastal Karnataka region, introducing a dedicated tourism policy for the coastal areas to treats tourism projects as infrastructure initiatives while offering investors special incentives and extended loan repayment windows.Additionally, the government approved the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology Policy, 2026-31, which paves the way for upgrading the existing fisheries college into the Fisheries, Marine and Blue Economy University and expanding its student intake from 60 to 200 seats.Beyond these policies, the administration unveiled new urban development planning, fisheries sector incentives, and major financial allocations totaling around Rs 32,611 crore—split evenly between rural development and regional growth for Mangaluru, Udupi, and the coastal region.The announcements further included plans to hold decentralised Cabinet meetings across 10 to 12 locations in the state over the next 15 months and the sanctioning of a new medical college worth approximately Rs 450 crore for the region.
Article Summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar announced Tulu would be recognised as an additional administrative language. Tulu is spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts. 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore.

Article Title: Morning-after pills may get 4 boxed warnings
Article Text:
The proposed warnings will also caution that frequent use may lead to side effects

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Morning-after pills containing levonorgestrel may soon carry four prominent boxed warnings. Govt has proposed that the pills should be labelled clearly as meant only for emergency use, not as regular contraception, not as abortion pills and not as protection against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections.The proposed warnings will also caution that frequent use may lead to side effects and advise users seeking regular contraception to visit a health facility or a registered medical practitioner.Dr Megha Tiwari, Consultant, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Kailash Hospital & Neuro Institute, said emergency contraceptive pills are an important and safe option when used appropriately, but concerns arise when they start being treated as routine contraception. "We do see women taking it repeatedly after unprotected intercourse, sometimes without understanding that it can disturb the menstrual cycle and cause temporary bleeding irregularities, nausea or anxiety around a delayed period," she said."The bigger issue is misinformation. Some women believe the pill can terminate an existing pregnancy, while others assume it offers protection against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections, which it does not," Tiwari said.She added that the proposed warnings were less about creating fear around emergency contraception and more about ensuring women understood its correct role as a backup method after contraceptive failure, rather than a replacement for regular contraception or condoms.The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed the changes through a draft amendment to Drugs Rules, 1945, covering levonorgestrel tablets of 0.75 mg and 1.5 mg. The warnings would have to appear prominently both on the packaging and the package insert.The proposal also seeks to add levonorgestrel tablets 0.75 mg and 1.5 mg as a specific entry under Schedule K of Drugs Rules, along with conditions relating to their exemption from sale-licence requirements.However, the warnings are not yet mandatory. The notification is a draft, with 30 days invited for objections and suggestions.
Article Summary: The proposed warnings will also caution that frequent use may lead to side effects. The warnings would have to appear prominently both on the packaging and the package insert. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed the changes through a draft amendment to Drugs Rules, 1945.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi Saturday questioned the narrative in which the responsibility for carbon emissions is pinned on developing countries while Western countries are absolved of their role as historical polluters, even as he reaffirmed the country’s commitment to climate action and stressed that it has the best record among G20 countries. “In developed countries, per capita carbon emissions are six times higher than India’s... India presents this fact strongly on global platforms... We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along,” he said. His remarks at an international conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’, organised by NGT, come as the world gears up for the global climate conference scheduled for Nov in Turkiye.He said India is providing solutions to modern climate challenges even as its per capita carbon emissions are less than half of the global average.The PM’s remarks are being seen as a pushback against the West’s attempt, despite its historical responsibility for alarming emission levels, to suggest that India needs to accept stiff emission-reduction targets. India’s cumulative (1751-2024) contribution to overall carbon emissions is merely 3.5%, compared with 23.5% for US, 15.4% for China, 6.6% for Russia, 5.1% for Germany, and 4.3% for UK.Though India is currently the third-largest emitter, its per capita emission, as Modi underlined, at 2.2 tonnes per person per year, is less than half of the global average (4.7 tonnes per person per year) and six times less than the per capita emission of US (14.2 tonnes) and Russia (14 tonnes).India has always raised these points at all multilateral forums, pointing to equity and importance of a cut in emissions by big polluters who developed by burning fossil fuels over the past two centuries, which led to global warming. India, however, has never deviated from its responsibility and has fulfilled climate action pledges under the Paris Agreement.“India is the only country in G20 that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP21 summit in Paris (in 2015), and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of ‘Hindustan’ that I am talking about. On every parameter — non-fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions — India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide,” said PM Modi while urging the gathering of jurists, academicians, policymakers, scientists, environmental experts and other stakeholders from 17 countries across the world to look at the figures.Looking ahead to COP31, scheduled for Nov in Antalya, Turkey, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav said India will continue to advocate climate action centred on equity, implementation and the needs of vulnerable countries.

Article Title: ‘Drought, extreme heat, wildfires’: 180+ scientists sound alarm over ‘super’ El Nino
Article Text:
Super El Nino

NEW DELHI: With India’s monsoon season ending on a rain-deficit note, more than 180 scientists and ecologists have issued an urgent appeal to prepare for what they warn could be an exceptionally strong El Nino. They have flagged risks ranging from drought and extreme heat to wildfires and damage to ecosystems.The appeal comes as the southwest monsoon begins its annual retreat. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) earlier on said that the monsoon had withdrawn from parts of West Rajasthan and conditions were favourable for further withdrawal from parts of Rajasthan, Punjab, Saurashtra and Kutch over the next three to four days.India has recorded a 15 per cent rainfall deficit between June 4 and September 19, according to IMD data. The Southern Peninsula has recorded the largest shortfall at 29 per cent. June saw a 35 per cent deficit, while July was the only month to record above-average rainfall. August rainfall stood at 213.3 mm, the seventh-lowest for the month since 2001.The scientists said the warning signs of El Nino were already evident in the tropical Pacific, where sea-surface temperatures have risen above the 0.5°C threshold and crossed 2.6°C in August.Projections cited in their appeal indicate anomalies could rise above 4°C.Earlier this month, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said prevailing El Nino conditions were likely to intensify into “a very strong event” in the coming months and persist through February 2027.The scientists urged researchers to use the advance warning to expand monitoring and document changes across India’s ecosystems.“We call upon fellow ecologists to respond by strengthening and expanding our research and monitoring efforts to better understand the effects of extreme climate events on the natural world and connected social systems,” they said.They warned that a strong El Nino could bring drought and extreme heat, putting pressure on farmers, fishermen and shepherds. They also flagged coral bleaching and mortality, more wildfires and the loss of large rainforest trees.The appeal also highlighted less visible ecological changes, including shifts in animal behaviour and delayed fruit production.“In addition though, more subtle impacts on India's nature -- including delayed fruit production or changes in animal behaviour -- could be equally important, but may be much less visible unless you are specifically looking for them,” the signatories said.Roxy Mathew Koll, a climate scientist with the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, told news agency PTI that the coming period should be used to both track and protect vulnerable ecosystems.“We must document these changes as they unfold, but also safeguard the ecosystems that remain and reduce the pressures already weakening them,” Koll said. “What we learn and protect during this El Nino can help India prepare for a warmer and more volatile future.”
Article Summary: India has recorded a 15 per cent rainfall deficit between June 4 and September 19. The Southern Peninsula has recorded the largest shortfall at 29 per cent. August rainfall stood at 213.3 mm, the seventh-lowest for the month since 2001. The scientists urged researchers to use the advance warning to expand monitoring and document changes across India's ecosystems.

Article Title: ‘Resist him forcefully’: Congress hits back at Trump over Russia sanctions law

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday said the only way to counter a “bully” was to “resist him forcefully”, after US president Donald Trump signed into law a legislation expanding sanctions on Russia and Iran and giving Washington new tariff powers targeting major buyers of Russian energy.AICC general secretary Jairam Ramesh made the remarks in a post on X after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on Friday. The White House said the law authorises and expands sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran.“The only way to counter a bully is to resist him forcefully,” Ramesh said.The legislation gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from countries that meet specified criteria linked to purchases of Russian crude oil or natural gas and sanctions evasion. It also targets Russian officials, financial institutions, defence networks and the country’s so-called “shadow fleet”.The measure does not automatically impose a 100 per cent tariff on any specific country, with the law giving Trump discretion over its implementation.Earlier on Wednesday, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the threat of up to 100 per cent US tariffs on Indian goods showed the government’s foreign and trade policies had “miserably failed”.He said, “The threat of up to 100 per cent US tariffs on Indian goods shows how the Modi govt's foreign and trade policies have miserably failed.” Kharge also claimed the government had agreed to a trade framework expanding US access to Indian agriculture, alleging it “mortgag[ed] the interests of our farmers”.The legislation comes as India continues to face questions over its purchases of Russian energy. The ministry of external affairs said New Delhi’s energy sourcing decisions are guided by national interest.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal earlier said meeting the requirements of India’s 1.4 billion people remained an “imperative”.“When it comes to energy sourcing, it is based on our national interest. We have said that meeting the energy requirements of our 1.4 billion people is an imperative that we have to follow. And we continue to buy energy from diversified sources,” Jaiswal said.On the new US law, Jaiswal said India had already conveyed its concerns to senior levels of the US administration.“As we have stated, at senior levels of the US administration, we have conveyed the implications that this legislation could have on India's energy security, for international energy markets, and for the overall bilateral relationship. I don't have anything further to add at this point,” he said.The White House said Trump signed the legislation on September 18. The law extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five years and expands measures against Russia’s energy and financial sectors.

It brought together Indian-American technology leaders from the Greater Seattle area to discuss ways to strengthen the India-US technology partnership.Addressing the event, Nadella said he was proud to have watched the Seattle technology community grow over roughly 35 years and was pleased to see it forming and strengthening its relationship with India, the consulate said.He described artificial intelligence as a general-purpose technology whose benefits would depend on its broad diffusion across countries, communities and sectors.The forum brought together technology leaders working across AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, aerospace and enterprise software.Participants included executives from Microsoft, Amazon, Boeing, OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel, Veeam Software, Helion, Rhythms AI, Zenoti, Anicca Data and SeekOut, among others. Article Title: SC questions alcohol prohibition law, points to 5 'evils'
Article Text:
Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor

NEW DELHI: Questioning the efficacy of prohibition, Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor - revenue loss, money spent on its enforcement, corruption in police, illegal distilling, and result-ant drug menace - while also referring to a number of hooch tragedies in Gujarat and other states over the years.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules restricting purchase of methanol and making it mandatory to add bitterant and colourant to it before selling to non-drug manufacturers. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.While allowing the plea of various chemical manufacturing companies, including Indian Chemical Council, the bench dwelled upon the efficacy of the prohibition policy. The court said recent hooch tragedies in Bhavnagar (Gujarat) and Sagar (MP), which claimed 13 and 15 lives respectively, were a reminder for the authorities to wake up and act."History bears eloquent testimony to the fact that complete alcohol ban often drives the liquor trade underground, increasing the prevalence of unregulated, lethal brews. The state of Gujarat has a strict prohibition policy... It has witnessed at least 10 major mass hooch tragedies since the state's formation and independence, claiming the lives of over 600 people," the bench said.SC rejected Maharashtra govt's plea and said the rules had no rational nexus with the objective sought to be achieved to prevent hooch tragedies. The court said it was not doubting the intention of the state but intention solely would not pass the test of manifest arbitrariness."The state failed to indicate that this practice of putting such additives would discourage or rather dissuade continuous usage of methanol or affect its chemical composition so it cannot be used in making spurious liquor. Further, the state has also failed to indicate how mixing of the additives would definitively prevent deaths. Another question that is left unanswered is how the respondent plans to prevent manufacturing of spurious liquor by the use of other adulterants," the bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.

Nila Vikhe Patil, daughter of Maharashtra educationist Ashok Vikhe Patil, was elected to the Swedish Parliament on Saturday from the Stockholm City constituency.Nila is the great-granddaughter of the founder of Asia’s first cooperative sugar factory, Vithalrao Vikhe Patil, and granddaughter of late Union minister Balasaheb Vikhe Patil. Her uncle, Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, is a Maharashtra minister.Born in Sweden, Nila spent her early years in Ahmednagar, Maharashtra. She holds a bachelor’s degree and an MBA from the Gothenburg School of Business, with Economics and Law, and also studied for an MBA at the University of Complutense in Madrid.Since 2020, she has worked at PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), a global services network, offering strategy, management, technology and risk consulting.In April 2025, she became an authorised public accountant.She has been a member of the Stockholm City Council. She also served as a political adviser in the Swedish Prime Minister’s Office, focusing on finance, taxes and housing during the Stefan Lofven administration.“It feels nice to be a part of the 349-member Parliament. I am looking forward to contributing to the city and the country,” Nila told news agency PTI.“I would like to be a voice for those who cannot vote,” she said. “I want to contribute to a society where every child gets a chance for a good future. We need a habitable planet with clean water, living nature and as few human-caused natural disasters as possible,” she added.The 41-year-old Nila said that she loves India dearly and misses her grandfather a lot.“I hope to make my grandfather proud. He made me read the state budget when I was 15,” Nila said.“I love India dearly and I feel very connected. I have lots of close Indian friends. I miss my grandfather a lot. He used to call me almost weekly during his last years,” she added.Sweden’s left-leaning opposition won a narrow majority in the September 13 election. The Swedish Election Authority said the four opposition parties won 176 seats in the 349-seat Riksdag (Parliament). The four parties that make up or support the outgoing conservative-led government took 173 seats.The opposition Green Party is focused on environmentalism, renewable energy and green politics.Nila has been active in the Green Party for 25 years and is a member of the Election Committee of the Stockholm Green Party.
Article Summary: Nila Vikhe Patil was elected to the Swedish Parliament on Saturday. She holds a bachelor’s degree and an MBA from the Gothenburg School of Business. The 41-year-old Nila said that she loves India dearly and misses her grandfather a lot.

NEW DELHI: “Sell your wife/do anything, just repay this,” read a WhatsApp message cited in an FIR filed by a senior executive who allegedly lost over Rs 1.2 crore in a fraud racket involving Yuvraj Singh Manchanda’s former colleague Anya Vats and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva.Police are now probing whether Manchanda, who was allegedly killed by the couple in Gurgaon on Sept 6, had learnt about their alleged activities.Police have found that the couple allegedly targeted people close to them, including a former schoolmate of Sachdeva, who was duped of over Rs 1.2 crore after receiving a fake Enforcement Directorate notice. The cheating case was registered at Parliament Street police station this August.The complainant, a senior vice-president at a non-banking financial company that is a subsidiary of a public sector bank, told police that the extortion began in Sept 2024, when he received the fraudulent notice on WhatsApp allegedly involving an acquaintance.According to the complainant, Sachdeva, a former schoolmate, along with Vats, allegedly claimed to have high-level government connections and offered to settle the matter.The duo allegedly also used fabricated notices in the name of the Union home ministry, citing fake cases under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, to coerce him into transferring money.The complainant allegedly transferred over Rs 1.2 crore primarily to Vats’ bank account, using his personal savings, loans and family borrowings.Vats later allegedly demanded another Rs 26 crore, claiming that Rs 13.8 crore had been paid to government agencies on his behalf. The complainant eventually realised that he had allegedly fallen prey to a fraud racket and approached police.In the FIR, the complainant also mentioned the WhatsApp message threatening him to repay the money before Diwali.Sources said Sachdeva had also allegedly duped his estranged wife over a property worth around Rs 4.5 crore in Greater Noida. A third case involved a domestic violence complaint filed by the wife.Police are now examining whether Manchanda had learnt about any of these alleged activities.The inquiry also revealed that Vats and Sachdeva had called Manchanda on the pretext of a client meeting on the day of the murder.A family friend of Manchanda said, “Yuvraj had informed his fiance that he was meeting the clients with Vats in 20 minutes and would call back soon.”Investigators have seized an illegal pistol and the victim’s car, and both are being examined by forensic teams.Electronic equipment, including the accused’s phones, has been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory to determine whether the couple had searched online for ways to dispose of a body.Cops have also found that the accused stopped in Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh, while fleeing to Uttarakhand after the murder. They suspect this might have been part of an attempt to dodge police.“They have been continuously changing their statements about the alleged monetary dispute with Manchanda,” sources said.“Vats claimed that the victim had threatened her, but no evidence has been found so far,” an officer said.Manchanda’s family has claimed that even on Sept 16, Gurgaon Police uploaded his entry in the “Unidentified persons found” portal on ZIPNET instead of “Unidentified dead bodies”. The body was found in Gurgaon on Sept 10.Gurgaon Police, however, said there was no delay on its part and Delhi Police should have lodged a missing FIR within 24 hours of receiving the information from the family.They should also have flagged it to Gurgaon Police timely, knowing that Manchanda worked in Gurgaon, said a senior officer.
Article Summary: Anya Vats and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva allegedly targeted people close to them. The victim, Yuvraj Singh Manchanda, was allegedly killed by the couple in Gurgaon on Sept 6. Police are now probing whether ManChanda had learnt about their alleged activities.

Article Title: World's last known wild Chilean tree daisy gets a lifeline as conservationists use ropes to support its only survivor and two seedlings arrive at a Scottish garden
Article Text:
Image: Wikimedia

World's rarest wild Chilean tree daisy clings to life

Scientists collect 29 seeds from the last known wild tree

Image: BBC

Two seedlings arrive at Logan Botanic Garden in Scotland

International conservationists work against extinction

Why scientists are growing the seedlings outside Chile

Conservation efforts offer hope for the species

A rare tree daisy from Chile's Robinson Crusoe Island is receiving a new lifeline after two seedlings arrived at Logan Botanic Garden in south-west Scotland. Dendroseris neriifolia has been reduced to one known wild tree, which grows on a steep cliff and is supported by ropes to prevent it from falling. Conservationists in Chile and the UK are working to preserve the species through seed collection and cultivation. In May 2026, 29 seeds were collected from the surviving tree and sent to Kew's Millennium Seed Bank. Eight seedlings germinated, and two have since been transferred to Logan, where specialists hope to learn more about their growth and help secure the future of the critically endangered plant.The remaining wild Dendroseris neriifolia tree grows on a steep volcanic outcrop on Robinson Crusoe Island. Its precarious position has made physical support essential, with ropes helping prevent the tree from falling. The species has experienced a sharp decline over several decades. By 1980, only eight wild trees remained. Reintroduction projects were attempted in the early 2000s, but the breakdown of protective measures in 2017 allowed invasive plants and grazing animals to threaten the site again.The Chilean tree daisy has been affected by widespread forest clearance, intensive grazing by introduced mammals, invasive vegetation and repeated fires.These pressures have damaged the natural habitat on which the species depends. Robinson Crusoe Island is part of the Juan Fernández Archipelago, a group of islands recognised for its distinctive native flora. The restricted distribution of Dendroseris neriifolia makes the loss of its remaining wild population particularly significant.In May 2026, conservationists collected 29 seeds from the surviving tree and sent them to the Millennium Seed Bank at Kew Wakehurst in England. Kew's analysis found that 25 seeds were potentially viable. Eight seedlings subsequently germinated. The work provides an opportunity to preserve plant material from the wild survivor and investigate cultivation methods for the species. The seed collection is part of a broader conservation effort that includes previous collections and restoration projects intended to support the recovery of the tree daisy on its native island. Though only a single wild tree remains, these eight young seedlings offer a hopeful first step toward securing the future of the tree daisy.Two of the germinated seedlings have now been transferred to Logan Botanic Garden in Dumfries and Galloway. The remaining germinated plants will stay at Kew and Logan is known for its mild climate, which allows it to cultivate plants from warmer regions. Its experience with species from the Juan Fernández Islands makes it a suitable location for growing the young tree daisies. Richard Baines, curator at Logan, said the arrival of the seedlings was a significant moment for everyone involved. He explained that the garden would provide a safe place for the plants while specialists learn more about their development and adaptation to different environments.The project involves conservationists and scientists from Chile and the UK. Jardín Botánico VerdeNativo, Chile's National Forest Corporation and the Juan Fernández National Park are among the organisations involved in the conservation effort. Diego Penneckamp, a scientist at Jardín Botánico VerdeNativo, described the work as a race against time. He said the international collaboration could help prevent the extinction of a species with a unique evolutionary history. Felipe Saez, a plant biotechnology engineer and administrator of Parque Nacional Archipiélago Juan Fernández, also highlighted the significance of the seed transfer for protecting the archipelago's native plant life.The seedlings at Logan and Kew provide a form of ex-situ conservation, which involves protecting species outside their natural habitats. This approach can help safeguard plants when wild populations face severe threats.Growing the seedlings to maturity could allow researchers to study their development and potentially produce additional seeds. However, the long-term success of the programme will depend on the plants' ability to survive, reproduce and contribute to future conservation work.The wider Dendroseris genus is endemic to the Juan Fernández Islands. Kew has also identified conservation concerns affecting other species within the genus, underscoring the importance of protecting the archipelago's unique biodiversity.The arrival of two seedlings at Logan Botanic Garden marks a new stage in the effort to preserve Dendroseris neriifolia. The wild tree remains on Robinson Crusoe Island, where ropes are helping protect it from falling, while its offspring are being cultivated in the UK.The project combines field conservation in Chile with seed banking and horticultural expertise in Britain. By maintaining plants outside the wild, conservationists hope to develop a stronger foundation for protecting the species and supporting its future recovery.
Article Summary: Dendroseris neriifolia has been reduced to one known wild tree on Robinson Crusoe Island. Conservationists in Chile and the UK are working to preserve the species through seed collection and cultivation. In May 2026, 29 seeds were collected from the surviving tree and sent to Kew's Millennium Seed Bank. Eight seedlings germinated, and two have since been transferred to Logan Botanic Garden in south-west Scotland.

Article Title: After Jantar Mantar setback, AIMPLB plans 3-month national UCC campaign, to take battle to states
Article Text:
(File photo) The All India Muslim Personal Law Board





NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board ( AIMPLB ) on Thursday postponed its proposed dharna against the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) at Jantar Mantar after Delhi Police denied permission, citing the "likelihood of a large gathering and difficulty in managing the crowd".The Board said it had assured authorities that the demonstration would be peaceful and described assembly and protest as constitutional rights. AIMPLB spokesperson S Q R Ilyas, however, advised supporters planning to travel to Delhi not to proceed, asking them to avoid inconvenience and maintain peace.The demonstration was planned to mark the Delhi launch of the Board's three-month 'Save India, Save Sharia' campaign, also described as its 'Movement for Protection of Constitution and Sharia', to mobilise public opinion on constitutional rights, religious freedom and Muslim personal law.At an "emergency" press conference, president Maulana Khalid Saifullah Rahmani, spokesperson Dr Syed Qasim Rasool Ilyas and general secretary Maulana Mohd Fazlur Rahim Mujaddidi criticised the denial and said the campaign would continue through other democratic and legal means. The Board plans to hold public-awareness programmes and legal conventions in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Kolkata and Bengaluru, besides reaching out to religious leaders of other faiths, civil rights groups and tribal communities.The Board has already taken its opposition to the UCC and Waqf law to court. After Uttarakhand notified its UCC on January 27, 2025, AIMPLB filed a challenge in the Uttarakhand High Court in February. After the Gujarat Assembly passed its UCC Bill in March 2026, the Board announced in April that it would challenge the legislation in the Gujarat High Court.Separately, AIMPLB moved the Supreme Court against the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, filing its petition in April 2025. The plea challenges the amendments on constitutional grounds, including Articles 14, 25 and 26 — the Right to Equality, Freedom of Religion (Individual), and Freedom to Manage Religious Affairs (Group).The Board also announced a comprehensive 'White Paper' documenting what it describes as "discrimination against minorities and violations of constitutional and religious freedoms", besides setting out its legal objections to the Waqf law. Its proposed charter will cover the UCC, religious freedom, protection of waqf properties and religious places, hate crimes, alleged unlawful demolitions and equal enforcement of law. It is to be submitted to President Droupadi Murmu, seeking protection of minority rights under Articles 25 to 30.The police decision came amid renewed scrutiny of restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar. On Thursday, the Delhi High Court questioned the police over its refusal to allow another proposed protest at the venue and asked how a blanket ban on demonstrations could be justified. The court was hearing a petition concerning a separate proposed protest by the Kshatriya Karni Sena.
Article Summary: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) on Thursday postponed its proposed dharna against the Uniform Civil Code. Delhi Police denied permission, citing the "likelihood of a large gathering and difficulty in managing the crowd" The Board said it had assured authorities that the demonstration would be peaceful and described assembly and protest as constitutional rights.

Article Title: From daily-wage labourer to entrepreneur: How Aajeevika Mission changed Sonbhadra woman’s life
Article Text:
Nirmala's journey in Sonbhadra showcases Aajeevika Mission's impact on rural women (AI image)

How

Aajeevika Mission

Transformed Nirmala’s Life in Sonbhadra

Aajeevika Mission: From women’s groups to

economic empowerment

Diversification creates a stronger livelihood

One woman’s success inspires an entire village

From self-reliance to market expansion

A model of women-led

rural development





In the tribal and economically backward regions of Uttar Pradesh, a quiet transformation is taking place. Women who were once dependent on agricultural work and daily-wage labour for household survival are increasingly becoming entrepreneurs, managing businesses and contributing significantly to their families’ incomes.The story of Nirmala, a Scheduled Caste woman from Bichpai village in Robertsganj block of Sonbhadra district, is a compelling example of this change. Once dependent on daily wages, Nirmala of Bichpai village in Sonbhadra now earns around Rs 2.5 lakh annually. Her journey from labourer to entrepreneur reflects how the Aajeevika Mission is creating new opportunities for women in Uttar Pradesh’s rural and backward regions.Once compelled to work as a daily-wage labourer to support her six-member family, Nirmala has today established a diversified rural enterprise. Her annual income has risen to approximately Rs 2.5 lakh, while her success has inspired nearly 12 to 15 other women in her village to explore livelihood opportunities and move towards self-reliance.At the heart of this transformation is the Aajeevika Mission, being implemented by the Uttar Pradesh government to organize rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs), build their skills, facilitate access to financial assistance and encourage them to establish sustainable livelihood activities.The basic idea behind the Aajeevika Mission is to ensure that rural women are not merely recipients of welfare but become active participants in the rural economy.Through Self-Help Groups, women are brought together and encouraged to develop savings habits, acquire livelihood skills, access financial support and undertake income-generating activities. The SHG platform provides women with a collective support system that can help them overcome one of the biggest barriers faced by poor rural households—the lack of capital and access to organized livelihood opportunities. Nirmala’s journey demonstrates how this approach can translate into tangible economic empowerment.A graduate, Nirmala had the educational qualifications to aspire for a better future, but her family’s weak economic condition limited her opportunities. Her family consisted of her husband, three daughters and a son. Despite managing household responsibilities, she was forced to undertake wage labour to supplement the family income.Joining a Self-Help Group under the Aajeevika Mission became the first major turning point in her life. Instead of remaining dependent on irregular wage employment, Nirmala was introduced to skill development and livelihood opportunities. She received training in candle-making, a relatively low-investment activity with strong seasonal demand, particularly during festivals.She decided to convert this newly acquired skill into an enterprise. Seed capital turned s a skill into a business. Training alone cannot create a successful enterprise unless women also have access to the resources required to put their skills into practice. This is where financial assistance under the livelihood-development ecosystem became crucial for Nirmala.Recognizing her initiative, the Udyamita Vikas Pariyojana provided her with Rs 60,000 in seed money as initial assistance. For Nirmala, this support became the starting capital for her enterprise. She used the money to purchase moulds for making candles in different designs and shapes. Rather than limiting herself to conventional candles, she began producing attractive, colourful designer candles in the form of flowers, trees and other decorative figures.Initially, she focused on the festival market, particularly Deepawali, when demand for decorative candles rises sharply. What began as a seasonal activity gradually developed into a regular business as customers responded positively to her products. The transformation is significant: the woman who once sold her labour for daily wages was now producing a marketable product of her own.Nirmala’s journey also demonstrates another important principle of the Aajeevika Mission—livelihood diversification. Instead of depending on a single product, she gradually expanded her enterprise into different activities. With support from the Khadi Gramodyog Department, she received a popcorn-making machine, adding another source of income.She subsequently received specialized training from the Food Safety and Food Processing Department. The two-month training programme equipped her with skills to prepare value-added food products such as rose gulkand, sharbat and gajar ka murabba (carrot preserve).Nirmala now produces these products according to seasonal demand. This diversification has helped her move beyond a single festival-dependent enterprise towards a broader rural business model. Designer candles provide opportunities during the festive season, while food-processing products create additional avenues for income during other periods.In this way, different government interventions have complemented one another—SHG mobilization, skill development, seed capital, equipment support and food-processing training—to help convert a rural woman’s potential into a sustainable livelihood.Household responsibilities no longer stand in the wayNirmala’s success also challenges the traditional perception that women in rural areas can engage in economic activity only when they are relieved of household responsibilities. She continues to manage her family while simultaneously running her enterprise.This is one of the important social outcomes of the Aajeevika Mission. When livelihood activities are designed around the circumstances of rural women and are supported with training, finance and local opportunities, women can combine entrepreneurship with their responsibilities at home.The result is not merely an increase in income. It brings greater confidence, decision-making ability and social recognition. For Nirmala, entrepreneurship has given her an identity beyond that of a wage labourer.The most powerful impact of Nirmala’s story can perhaps be seen in the women around her. Her success has encouraged 12 to 15 women in the village to move towards self-reliance. Her journey has demonstrated that entrepreneurship is possible even in a rural and economically disadvantaged area, provided women receive the right combination of training, institutional support and access to capital.This is precisely the larger objective of the Aajeevika Mission: creating an ecosystem in which one empowered woman can become a catalyst for change within her community. The transformation therefore extends beyond individual income. As more women join SHGs and take up enterprises, the economic role of women within rural households and communities becomes stronger.Nirmala is not stopping at her current achievements. Her next objective is to take her products to the online marketplace. This aspiration reflects the changing character of rural entrepreneurship in Uttar Pradesh.The journey that began with selling candles locally is now moving towards wider markets. Digital platforms can potentially help rural entrepreneurs overcome geographical limitations and connect their products with customers beyond their villages and districts. Nirmala’s ambition to enter the online market is therefore another important step—from local production to market expansion.Nirmala’s story illustrates the potential of a well-connected rural livelihood ecosystem.The Aajeevika Mission provided the institutional foundation by bringing her into the Self-Help Group network. Skill training gave her the capability to produce marketable goods. Seed money enabled her to purchase the equipment and raw materials necessary to begin production. Departmental support helped diversify her enterprise, while further training opened the door to food processing.The result is a woman who has moved from wage labour to entrepreneurship, from economic dependence to self-reliance and from individual struggle to becoming an inspiration for other women. Her journey also reflects the broader vision of the Yogi government to strengthen rural economies by empowering women as economic actors. In backward and tribal regions, where conventional employment opportunities can be limited, women-led micro-enterprises can provide an important alternative source of household income.Nirmala’s colourful candles may have been the first product of her enterprise, but they have come to symbolize something much larger—a new confidence among rural women. Today, Nirmala earns around Rs 2.5 lakh a year, manages her household and runs a diversified enterprise. More importantly, her story is encouraging other women in Bichpai to believe that self-reliance is possible.From a daily-wage worker to a rural entrepreneur, Nirmala’s journey is a powerful example of how Aajeevika Mission can transform skills into livelihoods, livelihoods into enterprises and individual success into a movement for women-led rural development.(District Transformation)
Article Summary: Aajeevika Mission is creating new opportunities for women in Uttar Pradesh’s rural and backward regions. Nirmala of Bichpai village in Sonbhadra now earns around Rs 2.5 lakh annually. Her success has inspired nearly 12 to 15 other women in her village to explore livelihood opportunities.

Completing it online ensures peace of mind and legal protection for homeowners.
